For Grown-Ups

Getting it on a tablet

Open https://atonachella.github.io/charm-island/purrch/ in the tablet's web browser. To keep it like an app: Chrome menu (⋮) → Add to Home screen (Safari: Share → Add to Home Screen). On a kids tablet with web limits, add atonachella.github.io to the allowed sites in the parent settings.

New versions show up at the same address. Progress is kept between versions. If an old version shows, close the game and open it again.

Graphics adjust on their own: slower tablets get softer shadows, a lower resolution and a shorter view distance.

Version 1.0

Purrch is a pretend pet game. Kids adopt cats and birds, name them, feed them, play with them, brush them and tuck them in for naps. Taking care of pets earns hearts, and hearts unlock new pets and rooms. At 25 hearts the Pizza Café opens: make a pizza, then deliver it to one of four animal friends (two live across a little hop-across course). At 50 hearts the 3D Printer Room opens: pick an animal mold and a color, then tap along to print it layer by layer. Prints go on a shelf and can be given to pets as toys.

Safe by design

  • No ads, no chat, no purchases, no accounts, no links.
  • The game loads once from its web address. After that nothing is sent anywhere: no tracking, no data collected.
  • Progress saves only in this browser, on this tablet.

Gentle by design

  • Pets never die, run away or get sad. Low needs only show a little thought bubble.
  • Sometimes a pet gets the sniffles or an ouchie paw. One tap on Help and they are all better.
  • Falling off the island just pops you back. Nothing is lost.
  • Pizza deliveries have a little hop-across course. Falling in the water just puts you back at the last flag. No timers, no game over.
  • Printing: a missed tap just makes a wobbly layer. Every print still finishes.

Games & Sister Link (the board button, top right)

Shell Mancala is the real two-row stone game. Kids play the computer (Easy, Medium, Hard) or each other, passing one tablet back and forth. Wins give a few hearts. Losing to the computer still gives 1, and rewards stop after 8 games a day.

Sister Link connects this game with Hook & Bead Cay with no internet at all. The game shows five pictures (like Moon, Shell, Leaf, Bell, Fish). Your kid reads them out loud and her sister taps them into her game. Codes carry gifts (3D-printed toys going out, bead bracelets coming in) and the weekly team board, where each sister finishes her half to earn a charm. 3 gifts can be sent a day. A code works once.

Print Bed Puzzles (Games button, top right)

A connect-the-dots puzzle game in two worlds of 12 levels. Drag across touching prints of the same color to clear them; close a square to clear every one of that color. Later levels add plushies to bring down, fur tufts to clean and boxes to break. Each level has a set number of moves and earns up to 3 stars.

There are no lives, timers or waiting. A lost level can be retried right away, as often as your kid wants. Stars pay out a few hearts the first time only. Kids can send a challenge code to their sister (level + moves left, five pictures read out loud, no internet), and she tries to beat it in her own game.

The world (Map, Quests and Book buttons, top right)

The game is now a small open world: five places joined by bridges. New places open by finishing quests for the characters who live there, not by spending anything. Friends with a ! over their head have a quest. The Quests button shows the current goal, and a soft light beam points the way.

There is a day and night clock (a full day is about 16 minutes of play) and simple weather. Some animals and finds only show up at night or in the rain. On the Map your kid can wait for morning, evening or night, and travel to any place already visited.

The Collection book fills in as things are found. Unfound entries stay as "???". Nothing here connects to the internet, and all characters are made up for this game.

Play time

  • 15 minutes before the daily limit, a heads-up appears. At the limit the island goes to sleep until tomorrow. Progress is saved first.
  • Only active play counts. Time sitting idle or with the tablet asleep does not.
  • Any grown-up can change the limit, turn it off, or add time for today. It asks a quick times question and a 2-second hold first.
  • This game keeps its own timer on this tablet. Erasing the game does not reset it.
